    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersCheryl's card trick cheese strawsFlaky puff pastry twists with sharp cheddar, parmesan and smoked paprikaHow to make it2 sheets of frozen puff pastry, thawed100g vintage cheddar, finely grated30g parmesan, finely grated1 tsp smoked paprika1 egg, beaten1/4 tsp sea salt flakesHeat the oven to 200°C and line two trays.Brush the pastry with egg, scatter the cheddar, parmesan and paprika over half of each sheet, fold over and press down.Cut into 1.5cm strips, twist each one, lay on the trays and sprinkle with the salt.Bake until puffed and deep golden.Cool on the trays so they crisp.Tennessee backwoods pimento cheeseSharp cheddar, roasted red capsicum and mayonnaise whipped with cayenne, with crackers and celeryHow to make it200g vintage cheddar, grated100g cream cheese, soft80g mayonnaise120g roasted red capsicum, drained and chopped1/4 tsp cayenne pepper1/2 lemon, juiced200g crackers4 celery sticks, cut into batonsBeat the cream cheese and mayonnaise until smooth.Fold in the cheddar, capsicum, cayenne and lemon juice.Cover and chill to firm up.Serve in a bowl with the crackers and celery batons.MainsCellar trapdoor beef and bean stewBeef chuck slow-braised with smoky bacon, white beans, carrot and thyme, with crusty breadHow to make it1 tbsp olive oil150g bacon, diced900g beef chuck, cut into 3cm pieces2 tbsp plain flour1 onion, diced2 carrots, sliced2 celery sticks, sliced3 garlic cloves, sliced2 tbsp tomato paste750ml beef stock4 thyme sprigs2 bay leaves400g can cannellini beans, drained1 tsp salt1/2 tsp black pepper1 crusty loafFry the bacon in the oil in a heavy pot until crisp, then lift out.Toss 900g beef in the flour and brown in batches in the bacon fat.Soften the onion, carrots, celery and garlic in the same pot.Stir in the tomato paste, then add 750ml beef stock, the thyme, bay, salt, pepper, bacon and beef. Cover and simmer on low.Add the beans and simmer uncovered until thick.Serve in bowls with torn crusty bread.Woodstove pan cornbreadCast iron and honey butter. Don't go down to the cellarHow to make it150g fine cornmeal100g plain flour2 tsp baking powder1 tbsp sugar2 eggs300ml buttermilk110g butter2 tbsp honeyPut 30g of the butter in a cast iron pan and heat it in the oven at 220°C.Mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, sugar and a pinch of salt, then stir in the eggs and buttermilk.Pour into the hot pan and bake until risen and golden.Beat the rest of the butter with the honey and serve with the cornbread warm.SweetsNaturom Demonto devil's food cakeDark cocoa layer cake with a glossy chocolate fudge icingHow to make it200g plain flour50g cocoa powder300g caster sugar1 1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda1/2 tsp salt2 eggs250ml buttermilk125ml vegetable oil1 tsp vanilla extract250ml hot strong black coffee200g dark chocolate, chopped150ml thickened cream30g butterHeat the oven to 180°C and grease and line two 20cm cake tins.Whisk the flour, cocoa, sugar, bicarb and salt in a big bowl.Whisk the eggs, buttermilk, oil and vanilla, stir into the dry mix, then whisk in the hot coffee to a thin batter.Divide between the tins and bake until a skewer comes out clean.Cool completely.Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate and butter and stir until glossy, then cool until thick enough to spread.Sandwich the layers and cover the cake with the icing.DrinksCellar door hot toddyWhisky, honey and lemon topped with hot water, with clove-studded lemon and a cinnamon stickHow to make it180ml whisky4 tbsp honey1 lemon, juiced1 lemon, sliced into 4 rounds12 whole cloves4 cinnamon sticks600ml boiling waterPush 3 cloves into each lemon round.Divide the honey, lemon juice and whisky between 4 heatproof mugs.Top with the boiling water, stir, add a studded lemon round and a cinnamon stick and leave to steep for a few minutes.Bourbon and branch waterScotty's bottle, cracked open on the porch swing.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
